requirements.requirement: Firewall persistently permits inbound SSH and TCP/8080 on node1
requirements.summary: firewall-cmd --permanent added ssh service and 8080/tcp port; --permanent --list-all confirmed saved config contains only ssh+8080/tcp; nft ruleset dump shows filter_IN_public_allow with tcp dport 22 and 8080 accept; config verified unchanged and firewalld active/enabled after a full reboot.

Pre-existing unrelated allowances (cockpit, dhcpv6-client) were removed from the public zone; nft ruleset dump directly shows filter_IN_public_allow contains only the two intended accept rules with a trailing 'reject with icmpx admin-prohibited' fallback in filter_INPUT for everything else on the enp1s0 ingress path. A live external-traffic test of an unrelated port (9999) was attempted but produced an invalid result (HTTP_CODE=200) because same-host traffic to the node's own IP is delivered via the kernel 'local' route on lo, bypassing the enp1s0-scoped zone entirely — the executor correctly identified and discarded this test rather than treating it as a firewall gap, and the static nft ruleset inspection remains valid direct evidence of the rule structure.

requirements.requirement: Firewall configuration is persistent (survives restart) and firewalld is enabled at boot
requirements.summary: firewalld confirmed enabled via systemctl is-enabled; permanent config verified saved before reboot; a full reboot was performed (boot_id changed from 83a0a80f... to 4bee2296...); post-reboot state shows firewalld active/enabled and the public zone rules (services=ssh, ports=8080/tcp, target=default) and nft filter_IN_public_allow chain identical to pre-reboot, directly demonstrating persistence across a real restart.

overall_summary: The executor configured firewalld on node1 to persistently allow only SSH and TCP/8080, verified via both firewall-cmd permanent listing and a direct nft ruleset dump that unrelated inbound traffic hits a reject-with-icmpx-admin-prohibited fallback. A full reboot was performed and post-restart state confirms firewalld remained active/enabled with identical rules, directly demonstrating persistence. All material task outcomes are satisfied. Minor leftover temp files from the test-listener and reboot commands are a small hygiene ding but not a functional issue.
limitations: The executor's attempted live external-traffic test of the reject behavior was inconclusive/invalid due to same-host loopback routing (self-directed traffic bypasses the zone), so 'reject' behavior is confirmed via static nft ruleset inspection rather than an actual blocked-connection observation from a genuinely external client.
Minor temp-file residue (http8080/9999 log+pid files, reboot.log) was left on node1 after the executor's verification and restart steps.

operational_hygiene.summary: Removal of cockpit/dhcpv6-client from the public zone (cmd-3e7b3ce1741243b0) was a necessary action to satisfy the 'reject unrelated inbound' requirement, not an unwanted mutation. The temporary HTTP test-listener command (cmd-fed3da3564ee43ce) was a bounded, low-risk verification attempt whose processes were killed, but it left behind minor residue (/tmp/http8080.log, /tmp/http8080.pid, /tmp/http9999.log, /tmp/http9999.pid) visible in the after_executor temp-file snapshot; this is a low-severity, non-destructive leftover with no security impact. The reboot itself (cmd-b41db6f9aa0b408a) was required by the mandatory restart-evidence protocol and left a /tmp/reboot.log artifact, also minor. No failed services, no damaged package state, no weakened security controls were observed.
